## 1. Purpose

This SOP describes the determination of cation exchange capacity (CEC)
and exchangeable base cations (Ca^2+^, Mg^2+^, K^+^, Na^+^) in soils
using the ammonium acetate (NH~4~OAc) saturation and displacement
method at pH 7.0 [@sumner1996; @chapman1965]. CEC quantifies the
total capacity of a soil to hold exchangeable cations and is a
fundamental indicator of soil fertility, buffering capacity, and
nutrient retention [@sparks2003].


## 2. Scope

- **Applies to:** Air-dried, sieved (< 2 mm) mineral soils from all
  EA Program sites. The method is also applicable to compost and organic
  amendments, although CEC values for highly organic materials should be
  interpreted with caution due to pH-dependent charge [@sumner1996].
- **Does not apply to:** Soils dominated by variable-charge minerals
  (e.g., highly weathered Oxisols, Andisols) where CEC measured at
  pH 7.0 may overestimate field-effective CEC. For such soils, a
  compulsive exchange method at field pH may be more appropriate
  [@gillman1979]. Does not apply to water samples.
- **Location:** EA Program laboratory, SGM 133

| Role              | Responsibility                              |

### Required Training

Students using this SOP should be trained on:

- [SOP-L400 Soil Moisture](SOP-L400-soil-moisture.qmd)


## 4. Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Chemical:** 1 M ammonium acetate (NH~4~OAc) is a mild irritant.
  Concentrated acetic acid used in reagent preparation is corrosive
  and produces irritating vapors. Concentrated ammonium hydroxide
  (NH~4~OH) used for pH adjustment is caustic and produces strong
  vapors. Ethanol (95%) is flammable.
- **Physical:** Reciprocating shaker can pinch fingers if containers
  are not secured properly.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
### Engineering Controls
Prepare 1 M NH~4~OAc from concentrated reagents inside a chemical fume
hood. Once diluted to working concentration, the solution can be used
on the open bench.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses or chemical splash goggles (goggles when preparing
      reagents)
- [ ] Laboratory coat
- [ ] Nitrile gloves
- [ ] Closed-toed shoes

### Emergency Procedures

For chemical spill or splash, refer to
[SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd) or call
campus safety. For acetic acid or ammonium hydroxide contact with eyes,
flush immediately with water for at least 15 minutes.

| DI water                        |                                          |


## 6. Procedure

### 6.1 Reagent Preparation

#### 1 M Ammonium Acetate (pH 7.0)

1. In a fume hood, dissolve 77.08 g of ammonium acetate
   (NH~4~C~2~H~3~O~2~, MW 77.08) in approximately 800 mL of DI water
   in a 1 L volumetric flask.
2. Adjust to pH 7.0 using dilute acetic acid (to lower pH) or dilute
   ammonium hydroxide (to raise pH).
3. Bring to 1 L with DI water and mix thoroughly.

::: {.callout-tip}
### Tip
Prepare this solution the day before extraction. It is stable
indefinitely at room temperature in a capped container. Verify pH
before each use, as CO~2~ absorption can lower the pH over time.
:::

#### 2 M Potassium Chloride

Prepare per [SOP-L403, Section 7.1](SOP-L403-nitrate-ammonium-kcl.qmd).

### 6.2 Moisture Subsample

A companion gravimetric moisture determination is required to express
results on an oven-dry soil basis.

1. Set aside approximately 10 g of soil from each sample for moisture
   determination
2. Dry at 105 °C for 24 hours and record the dry weight
3. Calculate gravimetric moisture content per
   [SOP-L400 Soil Moisture](SOP-L400-soil-moisture.qmd)

### 6.3 Ammonium Acetate Saturation (Exchangeable Cations)

1. Weigh 5.00 g of air-dried, sieved (< 2 mm) soil into a labeled
   50 mL centrifuge tube. Record the exact mass to 0.01 g.

2. Add 30 mL of 1 M NH~4~OAc (pH 7.0) to the tube. Cap securely.

3. Place on the reciprocating shaker for 30 minutes.

4. Centrifuge at 2,000--3,000 x g for 5 minutes. Decant the clear
   supernatant into a 250 mL volumetric flask. Retain the soil pellet.

5. Repeat steps 2--4 two additional times (three extractions total),
   combining all supernatants in the same 250 mL volumetric flask.

6. Bring the combined extract to 250 mL with 1 M NH~4~OAc and mix.
   This extract is used for exchangeable cation analysis (Ca^2+^,
   Mg^2+^, K^+^, Na^+^) by ICP-OES, AAS, or flame photometry
   [@helmke1996].

### 6.4 Ethanol Wash

The ethanol wash removes excess (non-exchanged) NH~4~^+^ from the
soil without displacing adsorbed NH~4~^+^ [@sumner1996].

1. Add 30 mL of 95% ethanol to the soil pellet remaining in the
   centrifuge tube. Cap and shake for 5 minutes.

2. Centrifuge at 2,000--3,000 x g for 5 minutes. Discard the
   supernatant ethanol wash.

3. Repeat the ethanol wash two additional times (three washes total).

::: {.callout-important}
### Critical Step
Incomplete removal of excess NH~4~OAc will cause CEC to be
overestimated. Ensure three full ethanol washes with clear supernatant
before proceeding.
:::

### 6.5 Displacement of Adsorbed NH~4~^+^ (CEC Determination)

1. Add 30 mL of 2 M KCl to the washed soil pellet. Cap and shake for
   30 minutes.

2. Centrifuge at 2,000--3,000 x g for 5 minutes. Decant the
   supernatant into a clean 250 mL volumetric flask.

3. Repeat steps 1--2 two additional times (three displacements total),
   combining all supernatants in the same flask.

4. Bring the combined KCl extract to 250 mL with 2 M KCl and mix.

5. Determine the NH~4~^+^-N concentration in this extract by
   colorimetric analysis (indophenol blue method), flow injection, or
   steam distillation [@mulvaney1996]. This value represents the CEC.

### 6.6 Cleanup

1. Discard spent soil in standard solid waste.
2. Rinse all glassware and centrifuge tubes with DI water.
3. Return reagents to labeled storage areas.


## 7. Calculations

### 7.1 Cation Exchange Capacity

$$
\text{CEC (cmol}_c\text{/kg)} = \frac{C_{\text{NH}_4} \times V_{\text{KCl}} \times 10^{-3}}{m_{\text{dry}} \times 14.01} \times 100
$$

where:

- $C_{\text{NH}_4}$ = NH~4~^+^-N concentration in the KCl displacement
  extract (mg N/L)
- $V_{\text{KCl}}$ = total volume of combined KCl extract (mL; typically
  250 mL)
- $m_{\text{dry}}$ = oven-dry equivalent mass of soil (g), calculated as
  $m_{\text{air\text{-}dry}} / (1 + \theta_g)$
- 14.01 = atomic mass of nitrogen (g/mol)
- The factor of 100 converts from mol~c~/g to cmol~c~/kg

### 7.2 Exchangeable Cations

Report exchangeable Ca^2+^, Mg^2+^, K^+^, and Na^+^ from the
NH~4~OAc extract (§6.3) in cmol~c~/kg:

$$
\text{Exchangeable cation (cmol}_c\text{/kg)} =
\frac{C_{\text{cation}} \times V_{\text{extract}} \times \text{valence}}{M_{\text{cation}} \times m_{\text{dry}}} \times \frac{1}{10}
$$

where $C_{\text{cation}}$ is in mg/L, $V_{\text{extract}}$ in mL,
$M_{\text{cation}}$ is the atomic mass (Ca = 40.08, Mg = 24.31,
K = 39.10, Na = 22.99), and valence is 2 for Ca and Mg and 1 for K
and Na.

### 7.3 Base Saturation

$$
\text{Base Saturation (\%)} =
\frac{\text{Ca}^{2+} + \text{Mg}^{2+} + \text{K}^{+} + \text{Na}^{+}}{\text{CEC}} \times 100
$$

where all values are in cmol~c~/kg.

### 7.4 Interpretation

| CEC (cmol~c~/kg) | Classification         | Typical Soil Textures       |
|:------------------|:-----------------------|:----------------------------|
| < 5               | Very low               | Sands, degraded tropicals   |
| 5--15             | Low                    | Sandy loams, kaolinitic clays |
| 15--25            | Medium                 | Loams, silt loams           |
| 25--40            | High                   | Clay loams, smectitic soils |
| > 40              | Very high              | Heavy clays, organic soils  |

Source: adapted from @sparks2003 and @brady2008.


## 8. Quality Control and Acceptance Criteria

- Include a reagent blank (NH~4~OAc and KCl through the full procedure
  without soil) in each batch. NH~4~^+^-N in the blank must be below
  the method detection limit.
- Run extraction duplicates on at least 10% of samples. Duplicate
  results should agree within 10% RPD.
- Include a laboratory reference soil with known CEC when available.
- Sum of exchangeable base cations should not exceed CEC. If the sum
  substantially exceeds CEC, suspect incomplete ethanol washing or
  analytical error.
- Verify NH~4~OAc pH is 7.0 ± 0.05 before each extraction batch.


## 9. Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                 | Container              | Disposal Method            |
|:---------------------------|:-----------------------|:---------------------------|
| NH~4~OAc extracts          | Drain with water       | Low hazard; drain permitted |
| Ethanol washes             | Flammable waste carboy | EH&S pickup                |
| KCl extracts               | Drain with water       | Low hazard; drain permitted |
| Spent soil                 | Standard solid waste   | Trash                      |

## 11. Training Record

Before performing CEC analysis independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
   training
3. Review the SDS for ammonium acetate, acetic acid, ammonium
   hydroxide, and ethanol
4. Complete [SOP-L400 Soil Moisture](SOP-L400-soil-moisture.qmd)
   training
5. Observe a trained operator perform the full extraction sequence
6. Perform the procedure under supervision with acceptable duplicate
   precision (RPD < 10%)
7. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager


## Appendix A: Example Calculation {.appendix}

```{r}
#| label: cec-calculation-example
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

# --- CEC Calculation Example ---

# Input values
nh4_mg_L    <- 42.5    # NH4-N in KCl displacement extract (mg/L)
vol_KCl_mL  <- 250     # Total volume of combined KCl extract (mL)
mass_air_g  <- 5.00    # Air-dried soil mass (g)
moisture    <- 0.032   # Gravimetric moisture content (decimal)

# Oven-dry mass
mass_dry_g <- mass_air_g / (1 + moisture)

# CEC in cmol_c/kg
cec <- (nh4_mg_L * vol_KCl_mL * 1e-3) / (mass_dry_g * 14.01) * 100

cat(sprintf("Oven-dry soil mass: %.3f g\n", mass_dry_g))
cat(sprintf("CEC: %.1f cmol_c/kg\n", cec))

# --- Exchangeable Cation Example (Ca from NH4OAc extract) ---
ca_mg_L      <- 85.2   # Ca concentration in NH4OAc extract (mg/L)
vol_ext_mL   <- 250    # Total volume of NH4OAc extract (mL)
ca_mw        <- 40.08  # Atomic mass of Ca
ca_valence   <- 2

exch_ca <- (ca_mg_L * vol_ext_mL * ca_valence) / (ca_mw * mass_dry_g) / 10

cat(sprintf("Exchangeable Ca: %.1f cmol_c/kg\n", exch_ca))
```
